_note: Standards named in wallcovering fire documents, and the reaction-to-fire class decoder. Editions and status are from BSI's catalogue records (metadata only: the paid texts were not read or reproduced). Class criteria are summarised from Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/364, Annex, Table 1 (as carried on legislation.gov.uk), and England's Approved Document B, Appendix B. sourceIds refer to sources.json.

standards.title: Fire classification of construction products and building elements. Classification using data from reaction to fire tests
standards.role: Turns the results of the reaction-to-fire tests into a class (A1 to F) with smoke and droplet subclasses.
standards.editionNote: Some older reports and declarations cite EN 13501-1:2007+A1:2009, which BSI shows as withdrawn in January 2019. A document citing the older edition is not automatically invalid; record the edition it cites and ask the maker if in doubt.

standards.title: Reaction to fire tests for building products. Building products excluding floorings exposed to the thermal attack by a single burning item (SBI)
standards.role: The single burning item test: a corner test that measures heat release, lateral flame spread, smoke production and flaming droplets for classes A2 to D.
standards.editionNote: BSI shows earlier editions current until these dates: 2002 to October 2010, 2010 to November 2014, 2010+A1:2014 to May 2020, and 2020 to January 2023. A report cites the edition used when the product was tested; record the edition it cites.

standards.title: Reaction to fire tests. Ignitability of products subjected to direct impingement of flame. Single-flame source test
standards.role: A small-flame ignitability test used for classes B to F; ignition of the filter paper below the specimen gives the d2 droplet subclass.
standards.editionNote: The 2020 edition was current until January 2026, so almost every report you will see cites 2020 or 2010.

standards.designation: BS EN ISO 1182 and BS EN ISO 1716
standards.title: Non-combustibility test; determination of the gross heat of combustion
standards.latestEdition: BS EN ISO 1182:2020; BS EN ISO 1716:2018
standards.role: Used only for classes A1 and A2. None of the wallcovering reports we read used them.

standards.title: Decorative wallcoverings. Roll form (2019); previously Decorative wall coverings. Roll and panel form (2007+A1:2011)
standards.status: Current at BSI; the 2007+A1:2011 edition is the one cited in the GB designated-standards list and the EU list
standards.role: The product standard for decorative wallcoverings, under which makers declare reaction to fire. England's Table 6.1 note refers to wallcoverings that conform to it.
standards.editionNote: The edition BSI treats as current (2019) is not the edition cited for UKCA and CE marking (2007+A1:2011), and Approved Document B also lists 2007+A1:2011. Declarations of performance normally cite 2007+A1:2011. Do not read one as the other.

standards.title: Reaction to fire tests for building products. Conditioning procedures and general rules for selection of substrates
standards.status: Current (the 2010 edition was withdrawn in August 2026)
standards.role: Sets the standard substrates products are tested on, which is why a classification names a substrate and holds only for substrates it represents.
standards.editionNote: Approved Document B still lists the 2010 edition, and existing reports cite 2010.

standards.title: Extended application on the fire performance of construction products and building elements
standards.role: Principles for extended-application reports, which assess whether a result can be extended beyond the tested build-up. England's guidance points to it.
standards.editionNote: Approved Document B lists the 2010 edition.

standards.title: Fire classification of construction products and building elements. Classification using data from fire resistance and/or smoke control tests
standards.role: Fire resistance of building elements, in minutes (for example EI 30). Not a wallcovering standard; listed here to keep the two ideas apart.

standards.title: Fire tests on building materials and structures: fire propagation (Part 6); surface spread of flame (Part 7)
standards.role: The British national tests, now withdrawn by BSI, behind Class 1 to 4 (Part 7) and the fire-propagation route to Class 0 (Parts 6 and 7); Class 0 could also be met by materials of limited combustibility.
standards.editionNote: Removed from England's Approved Document B from 2 March 2025; still referred to in the Welsh and Northern Irish guidance.

classes.label: highest
classes.meaning: The highest class. The product passes both the non-combustibility and the calorific-value tests. No smoke or droplet subclass is given.
classes.basis: BS EN ISO 1182 and BS EN ISO 1716.

classes.meaning: Passes one of the A1 tests to a less strict limit, and the single burning item test to the class B limits. Carries smoke and droplet subclasses.
classes.basis: BS EN ISO 1182 or BS EN ISO 1716, plus BS EN 13823: fire growth rate (FIGRA) up to 120 W/s, lateral flame spread short of the specimen edge, total heat release in 600 s up to 7.5 MJ.

classes.meaning: A limited contribution to fire growth in the single burning item test, and limited flame spread from a small flame.
classes.basis: BS EN 13823: FIGRA up to 120 W/s, lateral flame spread short of the specimen edge, total heat release in 600 s up to 7.5 MJ. BS EN ISO 11925-2: 30-second flame, flame spread no more than 150 mm within 60 seconds.

classes.meaning: As class B, with higher limits for fire growth and total heat release.
classes.basis: BS EN 13823: FIGRA up to 250 W/s, lateral flame spread short of the specimen edge, total heat release in 600 s up to 15 MJ. BS EN ISO 11925-2: 30-second flame, flame spread no more than 150 mm within 60 seconds.

classes.meaning: A higher fire-growth limit in the single burning item test and the same small-flame test as B and C.
classes.basis: BS EN 13823: FIGRA up to 750 W/s. BS EN ISO 11925-2: 30-second flame, flame spread no more than 150 mm within 60 seconds.

classes.meaning: Passes a shorter small-flame test only. May carry d2 if the filter paper ignites; no smoke subclass.
classes.basis: BS EN ISO 11925-2: 15-second flame, flame spread no more than 150 mm within 20 seconds.

classes.label: lowest
classes.meaning: Assigned when a product fails to attain class E. It is a class, not a blank: different from “no performance determined” and from an untested product.
classes.basis: BS EN ISO 11925-2: 15-second flame, flame spread more than 150 mm within 20 seconds (Delegated Regulation 2016/364, Table 1); England's Approved Document B, Appendix B, paragraph B6.

smoke.label: lowest smoke
smoke.meaning: The lowest smoke production category in the single burning item test.
smoke.basis: Smoke growth rate (SMOGRA) up to 30 m²/s² and total smoke production in 600 s up to 50 m².

smoke.meaning: More smoke allowed than s1, still within a limit.
smoke.basis: SMOGRA up to 180 m²/s² and total smoke production in 600 s up to 200 m².

smoke.label: no limit set
smoke.meaning: Neither s1 nor s2: no limit is set for smoke production.
smoke.basis: Not s1 or s2. Approved Document B: s3 means no limit is set.

droplets.label: none
droplets.meaning: No flaming droplets or particles in the single burning item test within 600 seconds.
No flaming droplets or particles that persist for longer than 10 seconds within 600 seconds.

droplets.label: no limit set
droplets.meaning: Neither d0 nor d1: no limit is set for flaming droplets. Also given when the filter paper ignites in the small-flame test.
droplets.basis: Not d0 or d1; or paper ignition in BS EN ISO 11925-2.

examples.reading: Class B; s1, the lowest smoke category in the test; d0, no flaming droplets or particles.
examples.note: It describes the tested build-up in the classification document, not the product on any wall.

examples.reading: Class B; s2, more smoke allowed than s1 but within a limit; d0, no flaming droplets or particles.
examples.note: The main class and the droplet result match B-s1,d0; only the smoke category differs.

examples.reading: Class C with no limit set for smoke or droplets.
examples.note: The class England's Table 6.1 gives for “other rooms”.

examples.reading: Main class B. The smoke and droplet subclasses are not stated, so they are unknown.
examples.note: Ask for the declaration of performance or classification report, which will state them.

examples.reading: Not a European class. A British national classification based on BS 476 tests, no longer used in England's Approved Document B but still printed in the Welsh and Northern Irish guidance.
examples.note: There is no automatic conversion to a European class; see below.
